p.seg: *Tíng Yún* ("Still Clouds")
*Tíng Yún*,
is about thinking of relatives and friends.
The vessels are filled with new liquor,
the garden arrays its early blossoms;
I wish to follow my desires, but cannot,
and my breast is filled with sighs.
Thick, thick are the still clouds,
dense, dense is the seasonal rain.
The eight regions are all dark.
The level roads are blocked.
Quietly lodging in the eastern window,
alone, I stroke the spring liquor.
My good friends are far away,
I scratch my head and stand for a long time.
The still clouds are thick, thick,
the seasonal rain is dense, dense.
The eight regions are all dark,
the level land becomes a river.
There is wine, there is wine,
leisurely drinking by the eastern window.
I wish to cherish my friends,
but boats and carriages cannot follow.
The trees of the eastern garden,
their branches flourish again.
All competing with new beauty,
to delight my feelings.
People also say,
the sun and moon are always traveling.
How can I quickly arrange a seat,
and tell them my life's story?
Lightly fluttering birds,
rest on the branches of my courtyard trees.
Folding their wings, they quietly stop,
good sounds harmonizing.
How could I have no other people,
but thinking of you is truly much.
I wish to achieve it, but cannot,
what to do with this regret!
*Shí Yùn* ("Seasonal Fortune")
*Shí Yùn*,
is about wandering in late spring.
The spring clothes are ready,
the scenery is harmonious,
accompanying my shadow, I wander alone,
joy and sorrow intermingling in my heart.
Slowly moving with the seasonal fortune,
quietly enjoying the good morning.
Donning my spring clothes,
I proceed to the eastern suburbs.
The mountains wash away the remaining mist,
the universe is warm with faint clouds.
There is wind from the south,
nurturing those new sprouts.
Vast is the level ford,
where I rinse and wash.
Distant is the far scenery,
filled with joy, I gaze upon it.
Speaking according to my heart,
people are easily satisfied.
Waving this cup of wine,
I am intoxicated and happy.
Extending my gaze to the middle of the stream,
distant and clear is the Yí River.
Boys and men together finish their work,
leisurely reciting and returning home.
I love their tranquility,
waking and sleeping, I wave my thoughts.
I only hate that we are in different times,
and cannot be chased back to.
This morning, this evening,
I rest in my hut.
Flowers and herbs are arranged in order,
the forest and bamboo are lush.
A clear zither lies across the bed,
a half-full pot of unfiltered wine.
The times of Huáng Táng cannot be reached,
I sigh that I am alone.
*Róng Mù* ("Flourishing Trees")
*Róng Mù*,
is about thinking of growing old.
The sun and moon push on,
and summer has returned,
I heard the Dao as a youth,
but have achieved nothing as an old man.
Luxuriant, luxuriant are the flourishing trees,
taking root here.
In the morning, they shine with flowers,
by evening, they have already lost them.
Human life is like lodging,
withered and weary for a time.
Quietly considering, I deeply think,
my heart is sad.
Luxuriant, luxuriant are the flourishing trees,
entrusting their roots here.
Flourishing and blooming in the morning,
I sigh that they will not exist in the evening.
Integrity and fragility depend on people,
misfortune and fortune have no gate.
If not the Dao, what to rely on,
if not goodness, what to strive for!
Alas, I, a small person,
possess this firmness and ignorance.
The passing years flow by,
my work does not increase as before.
I aim at that which I cannot give up,
how can I be content with daily wealth?
What I cherish in my heart,
makes me feel anxious inside.
The teachings of my former teacher,
how could I abandon them?
At forty, having no reputation,
this is not to be feared!
I grease my famous carriage,
I spur my famous steed,
though a thousand *lǐ* is far,
who would dare not arrive!
Gifting Grandfather of the Gōngzú Clan of Chángshā
*Zèng Chángshā Gōngzú Zǔ* ("Gifting Grandfather of the Gōngzú Clan of Chángshā")
The Gōng of Chángshā is my clan grandfather,
both descended from the Grand Marshal.
The ancestral ranks are far apart,
we have become strangers.
Passing through Xúnyáng,
I present this at parting.
From the same source, the streams diverge,
people and generations become distant.
Sighing with sudden realization,
I think of the beginning.
Ritual garments have long passed,
years and months have swiftly gone by.
Feeling for those on the road,
I hesitate and linger.
Oh, dignified and noble clan,
truly constructing this hall.
Harmonizing the air, winter is warm,
reflecting the emblems of rank.
I gather spring flowers,
and warn of autumn frost.
I say with respect,
truly the light of the clan.
I unexpectedly met you,
forgetting our differences in length.
Smiling and speaking was not long,
then parting to the west and east.
Far, far are the three Xiāng rivers,
surging, surging are the nine Jiāng rivers.
Mountains and rivers obstruct the distance,
but luggage and messages will sometimes pass!
How to express my heart,
I leave behind these words.
Though adding a basket of earth is small,
it will eventually become a mountain.
Respectful farewell,
sadly at the road.
Our hearts may be distant,
but our correspondence will be first!
*Chóu Dīng Cháisāng* ("Responding to Dīng of Cháisāng")
There is a guest, there is a guest,
who comes and stops here.
Holding upright office, he is wise,
and brings benefits to a hundred *lǐ*.
Dining with you is like returning home,
listening to goodness is like starting anew.
Not only in harmony,
but often having good companions.
Speaking and gazing,
to express my worries.
Releasing joy for a time,
drunk and then resting.
Truly happy to have a heart that understands,
now following me to wander.
*Dá Páng Cānjūn* ("Answering Military Advisor Páng")
Páng is a military advisor of the Imperial Guard,
traveling from Jiānglíng to the capital,
passing through Xúnyáng and gifting me.
Beneath the humble gate,
there is a zither and books.
Playing and singing,
I find my joy here.
How could I have no other likes,
but I am happy in this secluded dwelling.
In the morning, I water the garden,
in the evening, I rest in my thatched hut.
What people treasure,
perhaps still has not been cherished.
If there is no shared affection,
how can there be closeness?
I seek a good friend,
indeed, I find someone to cherish.
Our joyful hearts completely agree,
our houses are only neighbors.
I cherish him,
rejoicing in his diligent virtue.
I have fine wine,
I will enjoy it with you.
Then we present good words,
then we write new poems.
If I do not see you for a day,
how can I not think of you?
Our happy excursion is not yet over,
but we vow to part.
I send you on your way,
holding a cup, but without joy.
Lingering are the old mists of Chǔ,
distant are the western clouds.
You are going far away,
when will I hear your good words?
In the past, when we parted,
the orioles were singing;
now that we meet,
the sleet and snow are falling.
A great principality has given you orders,
to serve as an envoy to the capital.
How could you forget ease and comfort,
but the affairs of the king know no peace.
Gloomy is the cold sun,
whistling is its wind.
Lightly that square boat,
drifts gracefully in the river.
Strive, O traveler,
at the beginning, think of the end.
Respect this good time,
to protect your person.
《Quàn Nóng》 (Exhortation to Agriculture)
In the distant ancient times,
at the very beginning of humankind,
they were proudly self-sufficient,
embracing simplicity and containing truth.
Once cleverness and skill sprouted,
there was no means to rely on for sustenance.
Who would provide for them?
In reality, it depended on wise men.
Who were these wise men?
They were Shí Wéi Hòu Jì;
What did they provide?
In reality, it was sowing and planting.
Shùn personally plowed,
Yǔ also cultivated crops.
Looking back to the Zhou dynasty,
food was the first of the eight administrations.
Joyful are the sounds of commands,
luxuriant is the wilderness.
The grasses and trees flourish,
the gentle wind is clear and serene.
Crowded are the men and women,
rushing to compete with the seasons.
Silkworm-raising women travel by night,
farmers sleep in the fields.
The seasons easily pass,
gentle rain is hard to keep for long.
Jì Quē led his wife,
Jù Nì tied his plough.
Even those wise and achieved men,
were still diligent in the fields.
How much more so should the common people,
not stand with folded hands in long robes!
The livelihood of the people lies in diligence,
diligence then is without want.
Ease and comfort lead to self-indulgence,
what can one expect at the end of the year?
If you do not store up a little,
hunger and cold will come together.
Looking at your companions,
how can you not feel ashamed?
Kǒngzǐ indulged in morality,
considering Fán Xū base;
Dǒng Zhòngshū delighted in qín and books,
never setting foot in the fields.
If you can transcend this,
to find a high path,
how could I not gather my robes,
and respectfully praise your virtue and beauty?
《Mìng Zǐ》 (Instructing My Son)
《Mìng Zǐ》 (Instructing My Son)
My ancestors of old,
originated from Táo Táng.
Distantly, they were guests of Yú,
through generations, their glory was restored.
Yù Lóng diligently served the Xià,
Shǐ Wéi assisted the Shāng.
Reverent was the minister of education,
and his clan prospered because of it.
The Warring States were chaotic,
the declining Zhou dynasty was desolate.
The phoenix hid in the forest,
the recluse was on the hill.
The free dragon coiled around the clouds,
the fleeing whale alarmed the streams.
Heaven gathered the Hàn,
and cared for you, Mǐn Hóu.
Ah, the glorious Mǐn Hóu,
his fate was to climb the dragon.
Grasping his sword, he advanced early,
revealing his martial prowess.
His oaths were written on the mountains and rivers,
he opened up the land of Kāifēng.
Diligent was the prime minister,
truly following in the footsteps of his predecessors.
The vastness of a long river source,
the exuberance of a great tree.
Many rivers carry and guide,
many branches gather and arrange.
There are times for speech and silence,
fortune depends on prosperity and decline.
In our central Jìn dynasty,
our work flourished in Chángshā.
Magnificent was Chángshā,
his merits and virtues!
The emperor rewarded me,
giving me sole command over the southern states.
After success, I resigned and returned,
remaining uncorrupted even when favored.
Who would have said that this heart,
could be easily attained?
Reverent were my ancestors,
careful to the end as at the beginning.
Upright were the two platforms,
kindness and harmony extended for a thousand miles.
Ah, my benevolent father,
indifferent and at peace.
Lodging himself in the winds and clouds,
he was oblivious to joy and sorrow.
Alas, I am shallow and ignorant,
unable to reach such heights.
Shamefully looking at my graying hair,
I stand alone with my shadow.
Of the three thousand sins,
having no heir is the most urgent.
I truly think of this,
and heard your weeping when you were born.
Divination said it was a good day,
omen also said it was a good time.
I named you Yǎn,
and gave you the courtesy name of Qiú Sī.
Be gentle and respectful morning and night,
keep this in mind always.
I admire Kǒng Jí,
and hope you can aspire to be like him.
Having a son late at night,
you hastily seek fire.
All those with a heart,
why should I be any different?
Having seen him born,
I truly wish that he can become worthy.
People also say,
this feeling is not false.
Day passes and month passes,
gradually you are freed from infancy.
Good fortune does not come without cause,
misfortune also comes easily.
Rise early and sleep late,
I hope you will be talented;
if you are not talented,
then so be it!
《Guī Niǎo》 (Returning Birds)
Flapping their wings, the returning birds,
go from the forest in the morning.
Far beyond the eight borders,
they rest near the clouds.
If the gentle wind is not agreeable,
they turn their wings to seek their hearts' desire.
Looking at their companions, they call to each other,
their forms are sheltered by the clear shade.
Fluttering homeward birds,
Soaring and flying.
Though not yearning to wander,
Seeing the woods, their hearts are drawn.
Meeting clouds, they rise and fall together,
Calling to each other as they return.
The distant road is truly long,
But their innate love is without end.
Fluttering homeward birds,
Lingering in the familiar woods.
How could they think of the heavenly path?
Rejoicing to reach their old nests.
Though there are no former companions,
The collective sounds are always harmonious.
The air is clear at dawn and dusk,
Serene are their hearts.
Fluttering homeward birds,
Folding their wings on cold branches.
Wandering without straying from the woods,
Resting on the towering trees.
The morning breeze brings clear joy,
Fine sounds are often exchanged.
Why set up snares and arrows?
Having folded them away, where is the labor?
*Form, Shadow, and Spirit*
Noble and base, wise and foolish,
None do not strive to cherish life,
This is truly delusion.
Therefore, I fully describe the suffering of Form and Shadow,
And explain how Spirit discerns the natural to release them.
Good gentlemen,
May you all take this to heart.
*Seclusion on the Ninth Day, with a Preface*
I, in seclusion,
cherish the name of the Double Ninth Festival.
Autumn chrysanthemums fill the garden,
But there is no way to hold a wine offering.
So I simply enjoy the *jiǔ huā*,
Expressing my feelings in words.
Life is short, intentions are often many,
People rejoice in long life.
The sun and moon arrive according to the seasons,
The common people all love its name.
Dew is cold, the warm breeze ceases,
The air is clear, the celestial signs are bright.
Departing swallows leave no trace,
Arriving geese have lingering sounds.
Wine can dispel a hundred worries,
Chrysanthemums can control declining years,
How can a humble scholar,
Simply watch the fortune of the times decline!
I am ashamed that the dusty cup empties the wine vessel,
Cold flowers bloom in vain.
I adjust my robes and sing alone in leisure,
From this arises deep emotion.
Dwelling here is certainly full of pleasure,
Can lingering here not lead to accomplishment?
*Form Addresses Shadow*
Heaven and earth are eternally imperishable,
Mountains and rivers never change.
Plants and trees obtain the constant principle,
Frost and dew bring flourishing and withering.
People are said to be the most intelligent,
But they alone are not as good as these!
One sees them in the world,
Suddenly departing without a return date.
How can one not feel as if there is no one left,
How can relatives and acquaintances not miss them?
Only ordinary objects remain,
Raising my eyes, my emotions are sorrowful and overflowing.
I have no transformative art,
I will certainly not doubt you again.
I hope you take my words,
Do not casually refuse wine.
*Shadow Responds to Form*
Continued life cannot be spoken of,
Preserving life is always painfully awkward.
I truly wish to wander in the Kūnhuá mountains,
But that path is far and cut off.
Since meeting you,
I have never known different sorrow or joy.
Resting in the shade, we might temporarily part,
But stopping for the day, we will never separate.
Since this unity is difficult to make permanent,
We will darkly perish together with time.
When the body is gone, fame will also end,
Thinking of this, my five emotions are hot.
Establishing goodness leaves behind love,
Why not exhaust yourself in doing so?
It is said that wine can dispel worries,
But compared to this, is it not far inferior!
*Spirit Explains*
Great Creation has no private force,
The myriad principles naturally appear distinctly.
Man is among the three powers,
Is it not for my sake?
Although I am different from you,
I depend on you from birth.
Entangled in good and evil together,
How can we not speak to each other!
The Three Sovereigns, great sages,
Where are they now?
Péngzǔ lived to a great age,
But could not stay.
Old and young die the same death,
Wise and foolish are no longer counted.
Being drunk every day might lead to forgetting,
But will it not also shorten one's years?
Establishing goodness is always a joy,
But who will praise you?
Deeply thinking injures my life,
It is right to entrust oneself to fate.
Letting loose in the great transformation,
Neither joyful nor fearful.
What must end, must end,
No need for excessive worry alone.
Returning to the Fields and Garden
Six Poems
Poem 1
*Returning to the Fields and Garden: Six Poems*
From youth, I lacked a taste for worldly customs,
My nature has always loved hills and mountains.
Mistakenly falling into the net of the world,
Thirty years have passed in a flash.
A caged bird longs for the old forest,
A pond fish thinks of the old depths.
Clearing wasteland at the edge of the southern fields,
I return to the fields and garden, guarding my simplicity.
My square dwelling is more than ten *mǔ*,
My thatched house has eight or nine rooms.
Elms and willows shade the back garden,
Peach and plum trees are arranged before the hall.
Dimly, a distant village appears,
Faintly, the smoke of the settlement lingers.
A dog barks in the deep alley,
A rooster crows atop the mulberry tree.
The courtyard is free of dust and clutter,
The empty room has abundant leisure.
Long confined in a cage,
I have again returned to nature.
Poem 2
In the wilderness, there are few human affairs,
In the poor lane, few carriages pass.
In the daytime, I close my brushwood gate,
In the empty room, I cut off worldly thoughts.
Sometimes, in the village,
I part the grass and visit back and forth.
Meeting, we have no idle words,
But talk of how the mulberry and hemp grow.
The mulberry and hemp grow longer each day,
My land grows wider each day.
I often fear the arrival of frost and snow,
Falling and withering like the weeds.
Poem 3
Planting beans under the southern mountain,
The weeds are thick, the bean sprouts sparse.
Rising early, I tend the wild growth,
Carrying my hoe home by moonlight.
The path is narrow, the grass and trees long,
The evening dew wets my clothes;
Wetting my clothes is not worth regretting,
If only my wishes are not thwarted.
Poem 4
Long have I been away from wandering in the mountains and marshes,
Indulging in the pleasures of the forests and fields.
I try bringing my nephews and nieces,
Parting the brambles, we walk through the deserted ruins.
Lingering among the mounds and tombs,
I faintly recall the dwellings of former people.
The well and stove still have traces,
Mulberry and bamboo remain as decaying stumps.
Asking the woodcutter,
Where have these people all gone?
The woodcutter tells me,
They have died and disappeared without a trace.
One generation changes like the markets,
These words are truly not false.
Life is like an illusion,
Eventually returning to emptiness and nothingness.
Poem 5
In disappointment, I turn back alone,
Traversing the rugged, bramble-filled paths.
The mountain stream is clear and shallow;
I happen upon it and wash my feet.
I strain my newly brewed wine,
And with a single chicken, invite nearby neighbors.
As the sun sets, darkness fills the room,
Bramble firewood substitutes for bright candles.
Joy arrives, lamenting the shortness of the evening,
And already the sky is dawning.
Poem Six:
Seedlings are planted in the eastern highlands,
The sprouts fill the fields.
Though there is weariness in shouldering the hoe,
I take solace in the unfiltered wine.
At dusk, I cover the firewood cart,
The road is dark, and the light is already fading.
Returning people look toward the cooking fires,
Young children wait at the eaves.
You might ask, what am I doing?
In a hundred years, there will be demands for service.
I only wish for mulberry and hemp to flourish,
So that in the silkworm month, we can spin and weave.
My simple heart is just like this,
Opening the path, hoping for the Three Benefactions.
Asking the Envoy
"Asking the Envoy"
You come from the mountains,
Departing from Tiānmù (天目) Mountain early or late.
Below the south window of my house,
How many clumps of chrysanthemums have grown this year?
The rose leaves have already sprouted,
The fragrance of autumn orchids is about to be rich.
Return, return to the mountains,
In the mountains, the wine should be ripe.
"A Visit to Xié Chuān (斜川)"
On the fifth day of the first month in the year Xīnyǒu (辛酉),
The weather was clear and mild,
The scenery peaceful and beautiful.
With two or three neighbors,
We strolled together in Xié Chuān (斜川).
Facing the long flowing stream,
Gazing at Céngchéng (曾城) Heights,
The bream and carp leap, their scales shimmering at dusk,
Water gulls ride the gentle breeze, swirling in flight.
That southern hill,
Its name and reality are old;
I will not sigh and lament over it again.
As for Céngchéng (曾城) Heights,
Lacking support on any side,
Standing alone, outstanding in the central highlands,
I think of Língshān (靈山) from afar,
And cherish its fine name.
Delighted to see it, yet still unsatisfied,
I hastily compose a poem.
Grieving the passing of days and months,
Lamenting that my years do not remain.
Each of us wrote down our age and hometown,
To record the time and date.
At the beginning of the year, suddenly fifty,
My life is about to come to an end.
Thinking of this stirs deep within my heart,
And so, on this day, I take this journey.
The air is mild, the sky is clear,
We sit in order, leaning against the distant stream.
The weak currents carry swimming bream,
In the quiet valley, gulls cry and soar.
My gaze wanders over the distant marsh,
My eyes turn wistfully toward Céng (曾) Heights.
Though it faintly resembles the grandeur of the imperial palace,
Looking around, there is no comparison.
I hold the wine jug, greeting my guests,
Pouring full cups, offering and responding with toasts.
I don't know if from now on,
I will ever be like this again?
In the midst of the wine, I let my thoughts wander far,
Forgetting those thousand-year-old worries.
Let us enjoy the pleasures of today to the fullest,
Tomorrow is not what I seek.
Presented to Zhōu Xùzhī (周續之), Zǔ Qǐ (祖企), Xiè Jǐngyí (謝景夷), and the Third Young Master
(At the time, the three were comparing and discussing the *Lǐ* [禮], correcting texts)
"Presented to Zhōu Xùzhī (周續之), Zǔ Qǐ (祖企), Xiè Jǐngyí (謝景夷), and the Third Young Master, when the three were comparing and discussing the *Lǐ* [禮], correcting texts"
Burdened with illness, under the crumbling eaves,
The whole day passes without a single joy.
There are times when medicine and stones are set aside,
And I think of those dear to my heart.
The separation is not ordinary,
The roads are distant, what is the reason?
Master Zhōu (周) recounts the work of Confucius,
Zǔ (祖) and Xiè (謝) respond, impressively arriving.
The Way has been lost for nearly a thousand years,
And today, I hear of it again.
Horseback riding is not like lecturing,
Correcting texts is also already diligent.
This old man has something he loves,
And thinks of living near you;
I wish to instruct your sons,
Along the banks of the Yǐng (潁) River with me.
"Begging for Food"
Hunger drives me away,
Not knowing where to go!
Walking and walking, I arrive at this village,
Knocking on the door, clumsy in my speech.
The host understands my intention,
The gifts are not for nothing?
We talk from morning till evening,
Whenever wine is offered, I empty my cup.
My heart is filled with the joy of new acquaintance,
In speech and song, I compose a poem.
I am grateful for the kindness of the laundress of Piáo (漂),
Ashamed that I am not a Hán Xìn (韓信).
Knowing that I cannot repay,
I will repay you in the dark.
"Together with Everyone, Visiting the Cypress Trees by the Tomb of the Zhōu (周) Family"
Today the weather is fine,
With gentle breezes and the playing of strings.
Feeling moved by the people beneath the cypress trees,
How can we not rejoice?
Clear songs scatter new sounds,
Green wine opens cheerful faces.
Not knowing what tomorrow holds,
The feelings in my heart have already been exhausted.
"A Poem of Complaint in the Chu Style, Presented to Registrar Páng (龐) and Administrator Dèng (鄧)"
The way of Heaven is dark and distant,
Ghosts and spirits are vague and unclear.
Since I bound my hair, I have thought of doing good deeds,
Striving diligently for fifty-four years.
I encountered obstacles in my youth,
I lost my partner when I first married.
Flames have repeatedly burned me,
Caterpillars and water worms freely damage the central fields.
Wind and rain arrive in every direction,
The harvest is not enough to fill a small plot.
I embrace hunger on long summer days,
I have no blanket to sleep under on cold nights.
At dusk, I long for the rooster's crow,
At dawn, I wish the crow would move.
Since it lies within myself, why resent Heaven?
Sorrowful parting fills my eyes.
Alas, posthumous fame,
Is like floating smoke to me.
Full of emotion, I sing a solitary lament,
Zhōng Qī (鍾期) was indeed a wise man.
"Reply to Military Advisor Páng (龐)"
Reading your generous gift again and again,
I want to stop, but I can't.
Since we became neighbors,
Winter and spring have passed twice,
Our sincere and pleasant meetings
Have suddenly become old friendships.
As the common saying goes,
Several meetings create close friends.
How much more so when the feeling is even greater?
Human affairs are prone to discord,
And soon we will have to speak of parting.
What Yáng (楊) Duke lamented,
Is certainly not the only common sorrow.
I have been ill for many years,
And no longer compose literary works.
My talent was never abundant,
And now old age and illness follow each other.
I humbly follow the meaning of giving and receiving in the *Zhōu Lǐ* (周禮),
And consider this as a resource for longing after our separation.
Why must acquaintance be old?
Agreement can be determined at first meeting.
When there are guests who appreciate my interests,
They often visit my grove and garden.
Our conversations lack vulgar tones,
We speak of the sages.
Sometimes there are several *dǒu* of wine,
And we leisurely drink, naturally joyous.
I am truly a recluse,
And have no more connections to the east or west.
Things are new, but only people are old;
My weak brush says much.
My feelings reach beyond ten thousand *lǐ*,
But my body is stuck in this land.
Please cherish your health,
In what year will we meet again?
"Written on the First Day of the Fifth Month, Responding to Registrar Dài (戴)"
An empty boat is left to drift,
Returning again and again, endlessly.
Since the beginning of the year, time flies quickly,
Soon the astronomical cycle will reach its midpoint.
South windows rarely see withered things,
The northern woods flourish, rich and abundant.
A divine abyss pours out timely rain,
Morning colors herald a fair wind.
Since we have come, who does not depart?
The natural order of man must come to an end.
Live normally, awaiting its conclusion,
A bent arm, how could that harm the sky?
Transformations may be smooth or perilous,
Let your will roam without constraint.
Treat the present as if already elevated,
Why must one ascend Huá Sōng?
Drinking Alone in Continuous Rain
"Drinking Alone in Continuous Rain"
Existence arises, meets, and returns to nothing,
This has always been the way.
The world speaks of Sōng Qiáo,
But where can they be found today?
An old man offered me wine,
Saying that drinking can lead to immortality;
A first cup, and a hundred feelings fade away,
Another cup, and I suddenly forget the heavens.
How could Heaven be far from this?
Follow your nature, and nothing comes first.
Cloud cranes have wondrous wings,
In a moment, they can circle the eight points of the compass.
I have embraced this solitude,
Laboring for forty years.
My form has long since changed,
What more is there to say of the heart?
Number One
《Moving House, Two Poems》
I once wished to live in the southern village,
Not to divine a suitable dwelling.
I heard there were many pure-hearted people,
I would happily spend many mornings and evenings with them.
I cherished this desire for years,
Today I carry out this endeavor.
Why must my humble dwelling be vast?
Enough to cover my bed and mat.
Neighbors come from time to time,
Speaking frankly, we discuss the past.
Admiring rare writings together,
Analyzing doubtful points together.
Number Two
Spring and autumn bring many fine days,
Ascending heights, we compose new poems.
Passing each other's doors, we call out,
When there is wine, we pour and drink together.
Farmers each return to their work,
In leisure, we often think of each other;
Thinking of each other, we don our clothes,
Talking and laughing without tiring.
This principle is almost beyond enduring,
Do not suddenly leave this place.
Clothing and food must be provided for,
Diligent farming will not deceive us.
《Responding to Liú Cháisāng》
The mountains and marshes have long beckoned,
Why then do I hesitate?
Only for the sake of relatives and old friends,
I could not bear to speak of living apart.
A fine day enters my wondrous thoughts,
I take my staff and return to the western cottage.
On the desolate path, there are no returning men,
Often I see abandoned ruins.
My thatched hut has been repaired,
The new fields are ready to be cultivated.
The valley wind turns chilly and thin,
Spring wine relieves hunger and toil.
Though my weak daughter is not a son,
Comforting my feelings is better than nothing.
Restless in worldly affairs,
The years pass by, growing more distant.
Farming and weaving provide what is needed,
What more could I require beyond this?
Going, going, beyond a hundred years,
My name and body will vanish like shadows.
《Responding to Liú Cháisāng》
Living in poverty, I rarely use things,
Sometimes I forget the revolving of the four seasons.
In the palm courtyard, many leaves fall,
Sighing, I know autumn has come.
New sunflowers flourish on the north wall,
Fine grains nourish the southern fields.
If I do not enjoy myself now,
How do I know if there will be a next year?
I order my family to bring the children,
On this fine day, we ascend for a distant journey.
Number One
《Responding to the Registrar Guō, Two Poems》
Luxuriant is the grove before the hall,
In midsummer, it stores cool shade.
The gentle south wind comes in its time,
A returning breeze opens my collar.
I cease social interactions and idle pursuits,
Lying down and rising, I play with books and the qín.
Garden vegetables provide abundant nourishment,
Old grains are still stored for today.
Managing myself has a proper limit,
Surpassing sufficiency is not what I admire.
I pound glutinous rice to make fine wine,
When the wine is ready, I pour it myself.
My young son plays at my side,
Learning to speak, his words are not yet formed.
This matter is truly joyful,
I use it to forget the splendid hairpin.
Gazing afar at the white clouds,
How deeply I cherish the past.
Number Two
Gentle rains pervade the three months of spring,
Clear and cool is the season of pure autumn.
Dew condenses, there is no wandering haze,
The sky is high, and the scenery is clear.
The ridges rise with towering peaks,
Gazing afar, they are all wondrous and unique.
Fragrant chrysanthemums open, shining in the woods,
Green pines crown the cliffs in rows.
Cherishing this steadfast and beautiful form,
You stand out as a hero beneath the frost.
Holding a cup, I think of the secluded man,
For a thousand years, I caress your final words.
Examining plain paper, I cannot express myself fully,
Sadly, I spend the fine month.
《Seeing Guests Off at the Seat of Wáng Fǔjūn》
The autumn day is desolate and harsh,
All the plants have already withered.
Thus, in the season of treading on frost,
We ascend the heights to see off those who will return.
Cold air covers the mountains and marshes,
Wandering clouds suddenly have no support.
The islands and shores are distant and vast,
The wind and water are mutually contrary.
Looking forward to the evening, we desire a good banquet,
Parting words are truly sad.
Morning birds return in the evening,
A setting carriage gathers the remaining light.
Departing and staying follow different paths,
Turning the carriage around, I am filled with lingering sorrow.
My eyes follow the departing boat, far away,
My feelings vanish with all things.
《Farewell to Yīn Jìn'ān》
Yīn first served as a clerk for the Chief Secretary of the Jìn'ān Southern Prefecture,
and thus resided in Xún Yáng.
Later, he served as a military advisor to the Grand Commandant,
moved his family eastward,
and I composed this to give to him.
Good friendships do not last long,
One encounter exhausts all sincerity.
For two nights, we responded to pure conversation,
Increasingly knowing each other as relatives.
Last year, our homes were in the southern village,
Briefly serving as neighbors for a short time.
Leaning on our staffs, we wandered freely,
Staying long, forgetting night and morning.
Speech and silence naturally follow different paths,
I also knew we should be parted.
I did not think the matter would come so soon,
Now speaking in this spring.
Fluttering, the western wind comes,
Drifting, the eastern clouds go.
Mountains and rivers lie a thousand miles apart,
Laughter and words are difficult to make a cause.
Talented men do not remain hidden in the world,
The rivers and lakes are filled with lowly poverty.
If there is a convenient passage,
Remember to visit an old friend.
《Giving to the Commandant Yáng》
The Left Army Commandant Yáng,
is tasked to the Qin River,
and I compose this to give to him.
I, a simple man, born after the Three Dynasties,
earnestly yearn for the times of Huáng Yáo and Yú Shùn.
To understand things from thousands of years ago,
I truly rely on the books of the ancients.
The wise sages left behind traces,
all matters were centered in the capital.
How could I forget to let my mind and eyes wander,
but the passes and rivers are impossible to cross.
The nine regions have just been unified,
and I will soon prepare the boat and carriage.
I heard you are about to set out first,
but I am burdened with illness and cannot go with you.
If the road passes by Shāng Shān,
hesitate a little for my sake.
Give my best regards to Qǐ and Jiǎo,
how are their spirits now?
Who still gathers purple fungus?
The deep valleys must have been overgrown for a long time.
A team of horses cannot alleviate worries,
even poverty and lowliness have their joys.
Pure songs form a bond in our hearts,
but people are separated and fate seems distant.
Holding these thoughts in my heart for generations,
words cannot fully express my feelings.
*At Year's End, Responding to Vice Minister Zhāng*
The markets and courts are sad with the old people,
the swift steed feels sorrow at the Yellow Springs.
Tomorrow is not today,
at year's end, what more can I say?
A plain face hides its radiance,
white hair has already grown abundant.
How expansive were Duke Mù of Qín's words,
could his travels have been without fault?
As evening approaches, a long wind rises,
cold clouds engulf the western mountains.
The piercing cold becomes severe,
scattered birds return.
The lives of the people are rarely constant,
especially when entangled with sorrow and bitterness.
The arrival of pure wine is often delayed,
and there is nothing to enjoy this year.
Success or failure is beyond consideration,
emaciation is due to the changes of fate.
Reflecting on myself, I have deep thoughts,
and experiencing fate increases my lament.
*Responding to West Office Secretary Hú, Showing it to Judge Gù*
In the fifth month, when the season of ruí bīn arrives,
a clear morning breeze rises from the south.
Neither too fast nor too slow,
it gently blows on my clothes.
Heavy clouds cover the white sun,
and light rain falls softly.
My eyes wander to the western garden,
where the purple sunflowers flourish.
Now they are very lovely,
but how can they avoid decline?
Feeling moved by these things, I wish to seize the moment,
but I always regret not being able to do anything.
I idly wait for the autumn harvest,
which will be distant and delayed.
Unrestrained thoughts cannot be suppressed,
and I alone grow wild with sorrow.
*Lament for My Younger Cousin Zhòngdé*
*Lament for My Younger Cousin Zhòngdé*
With grief, I pass by your old home,
and tears of sorrow fall from my heart.
Asking for whom I grieve?
I mourn for someone in the nine netherworlds.
In terms of etiquette, you were one of my relatives,
and we loved each other as if we were born together.
When we held hands in front of the gate,
who would have thought you would fall first?
In the end, fate could not be avoided,
and you fell short of completing your mountain.
Our kind mother is immersed in sorrow and sick,
and your two children are only a few years old.
Two positions are left vacant in the empty hall,
and there is no sound of weeping morning and night.
Drifting dust gathers on the empty seats,
and overnight grass grows in the front courtyard.
The steps are devoid of traces of play,
and the gardens alone hold lingering feelings.
You have faded away, transforming into something else,
and will never appear again until the end of time.
Slowly, I will turn back,
my heart filled with sorrow.
*First Serving as Aide to the General Who Pacifies the Army, Passing Through Qū'ā*
In my youth, I lived apart from affairs,
placing my heart in the qín and books.
Gladly content in coarse clothing,
often empty, I was always at ease.
When the time came, I vaguely met the opportunity,
and reluctantly paused at the crossroads.
Putting down my staff, I prepared for a morning journey,
temporarily distancing myself from the gardens and fields.
A lonely boat departs into the distance,
my thoughts of returning are long and winding.
Is my journey not far?
Climbing and traversing over a thousand *lǐ*.
My eyes are tired of the differences in the river routes,
and my heart thinks of living in the mountains and marshes.
Looking at the clouds, I am ashamed of the high-flying birds,
facing the water, I am ashamed of the swimming fish.
My true nature was first in my heart,
who says my form is confined by worldly affairs?
For now, I will rely on the changes of fate,
and eventually return to Bān Shēng's thatched cottage.
One of the Poems
*Two Poems from the Fifth Month of the Gēngzǐ Year, Returning from the Capital, Delayed by Wind at Guīlín*
Walking along, following the road home,
counting the days, hoping for my old home.
First, the joy of serving my parents' warm faces,
then the joy of seeing my friends.
Rowing the boat, the road is winding,
the scenery is limited to the western corner.
How could the rivers and mountains not be dangerous?
But the returning son thinks of the road ahead.
The gentle south wind betrays my heart,
and I lower the oars, guarding the desolate lake.
The tall grasses stretch boundlessly,
and the summer trees stand sparsely.
Who says the guest boat is far away?
I can see a hundred *lǐ* ahead.
Extending my gaze, I recognize the southern peaks,
and sigh in vain, wondering what to do!
The Second Poem
People have lamented travel since ancient times,
and now I finally understand it.
How vast are the mountains and rivers,
it is difficult to predict the favorable and unfavorable directions.
The crashing waves roar like the sky,
and the long wind never ceases.
Having traveled for a long time, I yearn for my birthplace,
how can I be delayed here?
Quietly thinking of the goodness of the gardens and forests,
the human world is indeed worth leaving.
How many years are there in life?
Why hesitate to let your heart be free?
*In the Seventh Month of the Xīnchǒu Year, Returning to Jiānglíng on Leave, Traveling by Night at Túkǒu*
*In the Seventh Month of the Xīnchǒu Year, Returning to Jiānglíng on Leave, Traveling by Night at Túkǒu*
Living in seclusion for thirty years,
I have merged with worldly affairs.
Poetry and books deepen my old hobbies,
and my gardens and forests are free from vulgar feelings.
How can I abandon this and go
far away to Southern Jīng!
I tap the oar to the new autumn moon,
and bid farewell to my friends by the flowing water.
A cool wind rises as evening approaches,
and the night scene is clear and bright:
the sky is brightly vast,
and the river surface is brightly flat.
Burdened by the journey, I cannot sleep,
and I am still traveling alone in the middle of the night.
The songs of merchants are not my concern,
my heart lingers on plowing in pairs.
I will remove my hat and return to my old home,
not to be entangled by good titles.
Nurturing my true self under the thatched roof,
I hope to make a good name for myself.
One of the Poems
*Two Poems on Remembering the Ancient Rural Life at the Beginning of Spring in the Guǐmǎo Year*
In the past, I heard of the southern fields,
but I never actually set foot there.
Since there are people who are often empty,
how can my spring feelings be avoided?
Early in the morning, I prepared my carriage,
and my feelings were already drawn to the road ahead.
Birds sing joyfully in the new season,
and the cool wind sends forth remaining goodness.
Withered grass covers the desolate path,
and the place is remote due to the lack of people.
Therefore, the old man with a staff
leisurely never returns.
My understanding is lacking compared to those with broad knowledge,
and what I hold onto is certainly shallow.
The Second Poem
The late teacher had a bequeathed instruction:
"Worry about the Way, not about poverty."
Gazing afar, it's hard to reach,
I turn to resolve in diligence and hard work.
Holding the plow, I rejoice in seasonal tasks,
With a smiling face, I encourage the farmers.
Level fields intersect with distant winds,
And the good seedlings also harbor new hope.
Although I have not yet measured the year's yield,
I am pleased with many things at hand.
Plowing and planting have times for rest,
Travelers pass by without asking about the ford.
As the sun sets, we return together,
With a pot of drink, I treat my close neighbors.
I chant long verses, closing my brushwood gate,
Content to be a farmer in the fields.
Written in the twelfth month of the Guǐmǎo year for my younger cousin Jìngyuǎn
*Guǐmǎo suì shí'èr yuè zhōng zuò yǔ cóng dì Jìngyuǎn* (Written in the Twelfth Month of the Guǐmǎo Year for My Younger Cousin Jìngyuǎn)
My footprints are hidden beneath the humble gate,
Far removed and cut off from the world.
Looking around, no one knows me,
The wattle door is always shut in the daytime.
The bleak and cold year-end wind is sorrowful,
The dim and hazy snow falls day after day.
I strain my ears but hear no hopeful sound,
All that I see is pure white and clean.
The piercing air invades my sleeves and collar,
The simple basket and gourd I decline to set out.
Desolate in the empty space,
There is nothing to delight in.
Looking through books of a thousand years,
I often see the noble integrity of those who came before.
Their lofty virtue is beyond my reach,
But I deeply understand their resolve in times of hardship.
If I do not take the road to Píngjīn,
How can my humble dwelling be considered clumsy?
My meaning lies beyond words,
Who can understand this bond!
*Yǐsì suì sān yuè wèi Jiànwēi cānjūn shǐ dōu jīng Qián Xī* (In the Third Month of the Yǐsì Year, Serving as Military Advisor to Jiànwēi, I Passed Through Qián Creek)
I have not trod on this soil,
For many years now.
Morning and evening, I gaze at the mountains and rivers,
Everything is just as it was in the past.
A light rain washes the tall trees,
A fresh gale lifts the cloud wings.
I cherish the continued existence of these things,
The moral customs have not been isolated.
What kind of person am I,
That I should strive in this service?
My physical form seems to be constrained,
My plain heart cannot be easily changed.
Day and night I dream of my garden and fields,
How can I long endure this separation?
I always long for my returning boat,
I am indeed like a frost-covered cypress.
*Huán jiù jū* (Returning to My Old Home)
Formerly, my home was in the capital,
Six years have passed since I left and returned.
Today I have finally come back again,
I am deeply saddened by many things.
The paths between the fields have not changed,
But the houses in the village are no longer the same.
Walking through my old residence,
Few of the old neighbors remain.
Step by step, I search for past traces,
There are places where I linger especially.
In the flow of a hundred years,
Cold and heat pass day by day.
I constantly fear that the great transformation will end,
That my strength and energy will not keep pace with my decline.
Put it aside and do not dwell on it,
A cup of wine can dispel it for now.
*Wùshēn suì liù yuè zhōng yù huǒ* (Encountering a Fire in the Sixth Month of the Wùshēn Year)
My thatched hut is located in a poor alley,
Gladly rejecting luxurious mansions.
In the height of summer, a strong wind suddenly arose,
Instantly burning the woods and houses.
Not a single building remained in the whole estate,
Only a boat shaded the front door.
The distant new autumn evening arrives slowly,
The radiant moon will soon be full.
Fruits and vegetables are starting to grow again,
But the startled birds have not yet returned.
In the middle of the night, I stand and think,
A single glance surveys the entire sky.
From youth, I have embraced loneliness,
Suddenly, forty years have passed.
My physical form drifts with the transformations,
My spirit remains freely at leisure.
Integrity and firmness have their own essence,
Jade and stone are not truly hard.
I yearn for the days when I lived in Dōnghù,
When leftover grain lay overnight in the central field.
Patting my belly, with nothing to worry about,
I rose in the morning and went to sleep at night.
Since I have not encountered this again,
I will then cultivate the western garden.
*Jǐyǒu suì jiǔ yuè jiǔ rì* (Ninth Day of the Ninth Month in the Jǐyǒu Year)
The fading autumn is coming to an end,
A mournful wind and dew intertwine.
Creeping plants no longer flourish,
The garden trees wither in vain.
Pure air clarifies the remaining dregs,
The realm of heaven is distant and high.
The sorrowful cicadas have no sound of return,
Flocks of wild geese cry in the clouds.
The myriad transformations follow one another,
How can human life not be toilsome!
From ancient times, all have perished,
Thinking of this, my heart is anxious.
How can I express my feelings?
I will intoxicate myself with this muddy wine.
A thousand years from now is beyond my knowledge,
I will enjoy this present day.
*Gēngxū suì jiǔ yuè zhōng yú xī tián huò zǎo dào* (In the Ninth Month of the Gēngxū Year, Harvesting Early Rice in the Western Fields)
Human life has a way to return,
Food and clothing are its foundation.
Who is it that does not manage these,
Yet seeks to live in peace!
In early spring, I manage my usual work,
The year's efforts can be seen.
I go out in the morning to engage in light labor,
At sunset, I return carrying the plow.
In the mountains, there is abundant frost and dew,
The wind and air also feel cold earlier.
How can farm life not be hard?
But I cannot avoid this hardship;
My four limbs are indeed weary,
But hopefully no other misfortune will come.
I wash and rest under the eaves,
And scatter my worries with a jug of wine.
The distant hearts of Jǔ Nì,
Are connected across a thousand years.
I only wish it would always be like this,
I do not sigh at farming.
*Bǐngchén suì bā yuè zhōng yú xià xùn tiánshè huò* (In the Eighth Month of the Bǐngchén Year, Harvesting at the Field Cottage in Xiàxùn)
Poorly dwelling, I rely on agriculture,
Striving hard in the eastern forest corner.
I do not speak of the spring's toil,
I always fear failing what is in my heart.
The god of the fields cares for the harvest in autumn,
Sending a voice that agrees with mine.
The hungry rejoice at their initial fullness,
Girding their robes, they await the crowing of the rooster.
I raise my oars to cross the level lake,
Sailing and following the clear valley's bend.
Deep in the luxuriant desolate mountains,
The sound of apes is leisurely and sad.
The grieving wind cherishes the quiet night,
The forest birds delight in the opening of dawn.
I say that I came here,
When three or four stars were declining.
My appearance and years have passed and aged,
But the task has not gone wrong.
From afar, I thank the old man carrying the hoe,
And gladly find shelter with you.
*Yǐnjiǔ* (Drinking Wine)
Twenty Poems
*Yǐnjiǔ* (Drinking Wine)
I live in leisure with little joy,
And these nights have become long,
Occasionally I have fine wine,
And there is no evening when I do not drink.
I look at my reflection and drink alone,
Suddenly, I am drunk again.
After becoming drunk,
I often write a few lines to amuse myself,
And the paper and ink accumulate.
The words have no order,
So I ask an old friend to write them down,
To take it as a source of joy.
Number One
Prosperity and decline have no fixed place,
Each in turn shares them.
Shào Píng tilled melons in the fields,
How could he be like when he was the Marquis of Dōnglíng?
Cold and heat alternate,
And human affairs are always like this.
An enlightened person understands this meeting,
And will no longer be in doubt.
Suddenly, with a cup of wine,
We spend the day and night holding onto joy.
Number Two
Accumulating good deeds is said to have its reward,
Yí Shū was in the Western Mountains.
If good and evil do not correspond,
why establish words in vain?
At ninety, he walked with a rope,
how much more so was his hunger and cold in his younger years?
If he had not relied on the principle of enduring poverty,
who would have passed down his name for generations?
Number Three
The Way has been lost for nearly a thousand years,
everyone cherishes their feelings.
Having wine, they are unwilling to drink it,
but only care for worldly fame.
The reason for valuing ourselves,
is it not in this one life?
And how much can one life amount to?
It passes swiftly like a flash of lightning.
Within a bustling hundred years,
what can you achieve by holding onto this?
Number Four
Restless, a bird separated from its flock,
still flies alone at dusk.
Wandering without a fixed stop,
its sound grows sadder every night.
Its shrill cry longs for the clear distance,
coming and going, on what does it rely?
It encounters a solitary pine,
folds its wings and returns from afar.
There are no flourishing trees in the strong wind,
this shade alone does not wane.
Having entrusted itself, it has found its place,
for a thousand years, it will not stray.
Number Five
I build my hut in a human realm,
yet there is no noise of carriages and horses.
You ask me how I can do this?
When the heart is distant, the place becomes secluded on its own.
Picking chrysanthemums under the eastern fence,
I leisurely see the Nán Shān.
The mountain air is good at dusk,
flying birds return together.
There is true meaning in this,
I want to explain, but I have already forgotten the words.
Number Six
There are myriad ways of acting and ceasing,
who knows what is right and wrong?
If right and wrong take shape from each other,
praise and blame are the same!
The Three Dynasties had many such events,
enlightened scholars seem not to be like this.
Fie on the evils of the mundane world,
I will go and follow Huáng Qǐ.
Number Seven
Autumn chrysanthemums have a beautiful color,
I gather their petals laden with dew.
Floating this "forget-sorrow" plant,
I distance myself from the feelings of abandoning the world.
Though I drink a cup alone,
when the cup is empty, the pot empties itself.
At sunset, all creatures rest,
returning birds rush to the forest, chirping;
I whistle and stroll under the eastern window,
and manage to regain this life.
Number Eight
A green pine stands in the eastern garden,
many grasses obscure its rare beauty.
Congealed frost destroys different kinds,
its tall branches are distinctly visible.
In a continuous forest, people do not notice it,
as a solitary tree, people find it extraordinary.
Carrying a pot, I hang it on a cold branch,
and gaze from afar, repeatedly.
My life is like a dream,
why should I be bound by the tethers of dust?
Number Nine
In the clear morning, I hear knocking on the door,
I put on my clothes upside down and go to open it myself.
I ask, "Who are you?"
An old farmer has good intentions.
He brings a pot of wine from afar to see me,
suspecting that I am out of step with the times.
Underneath my ragged clothes and thatched eaves,
is not enough for a lofty dwelling.
The whole world esteems conformity,
I wish you would muddy yourself in its mud.
Deeply touched by the words of the elders,
my natural disposition rarely harmonizes.
Reining in the horse may indeed be learned,
but going against oneself, is that not delusion?
Let us enjoy this drink together,
my carriage cannot be turned back.
Number Ten
In the past, I once traveled far,
all the way to the corner of the East Sea;
the road was remote and long,
wind and waves hindered me along the way.
What made me take this trip?
It seemed I was driven by hunger.
Striving to fill my belly,
a little was more than enough.
Fearing that this was not a good plan,
I stopped my carriage and returned to a quiet residence.
Number Eleven
Yán Huí is called benevolent,
Róng Gōng is said to have had the Way.
Repeatedly impoverished, he did not live long,
and suffered hunger until old age.
Though they left behind a name,
their lives were also withered;
after death, what do they know?
Contentment is truly good.
The guest cherishes a thousand-gold body,
but upon death, his treasures vanish.
Why be averse to a naked burial?
People should understand the meaning behind it.
Number Twelve
Zhǎng Gōng once served as an official,
but his noble spirit lost its opportunity.
He shut his door and never came out again,
severing ties with the world for life.
Zhòng Lǐ returned to the great marshes,
and his lofty spirit began from there.
Once you leave, you should be done with it,
why be hesitant and doubtful again?
Having left, what path should one take?
The world has long been deceiving.
Cast off the idle talk,
and please follow where I am going.
Number Thirteen
There are guests who constantly stay together,
but their interests and choices are vastly different.
One scholar is always drunk,
while one man is sober year-round.
The sober and drunk laugh at each other,
their words fail to connect.
Being meticulous is so foolish,
being aloof seems rather intelligent.
I say to the drunken guest,
when the sun sets, the candle should burn brightly.
Number Fourteen
Old friends appreciate my interests,
carrying wine, they come together.
We sit on mats among the pines,
drinking repeatedly until drunk again.
Old villagers speak in a jumble,
the order of the cups and drinks is lost.
Without realizing we exist,
how would we know what things are valuable?
Leisurely, we are lost in what remains,
there is deep flavor in the wine!
Number Fifteen
My poor dwelling lacks labor,
and shrubs overrun my remaining house.
Clearly there are soaring birds,
but silently, there are no tracks.
How vast is the universe,
and human life rarely reaches a hundred.
Years and months urge each other on,
and the hair at my temples is already white.
If I do not entrust myself to poverty or success,
then cherishing my principles would be deeply regrettable.
Number Sixteen
In youth, I rarely dealt with human affairs,
my pleasures were in the Six Classics.
Walking and walking, I approach the age of non-confusion,
but lingering, I have achieved nothing.
I still hold onto the principle of enduring poverty,
and hunger and cold have often filled my days.
My dilapidated hut is filled with sorrowful wind,
and wild grasses have submerged my front courtyard.
Wearing coarse clothes, I guard the long night,
and the morning rooster refuses to crow.
Mèng Gōng is not here,
and he has completely obscured my feelings.
Number Seventeen
A secluded orchid grows in the front courtyard,
holding its fragrance, awaiting a clear breeze.
The clear breeze suddenly arrives,
and it is seen distinct from the artemisia.
Walking and walking, I lose my old path,
letting the path lead, perhaps I can get through.
Realizing, I should think of returning,
when the birds are gone, the good bow is discarded.
Number Eighteen
Zǐ Yún was by nature fond of wine,
but his family was poor and he had no means to obtain it.
He often relied on people who loved good deeds
to bring him wine and dispel his confusion.
He would drain the cup when it came,
and answer every question without fail;
sometimes he would refuse to speak,
but wasn't that akin to harming the country?
The benevolent one uses his heart,
how could he ever lose the distinction between showing and concealing?
Number Nineteen
In the past, I suffered bitterly from prolonged hunger,
so I abandoned the plow and went to study for office.
Because I did not control my diet,
cold and hunger firmly gripped me.
At that time, I was approaching thirty,
and my aspirations and intentions were often cause for shame.
Therefore, I exhausted my meager portion,
and will return to the fields and villages to die.
Slowly, the starry influences flow,
and a full cycle of twelve years has passed.
The path of the world is vast and distant,
which is why Yáng Zhū stopped.
Although there are no deeds of scattering gold,
I can at least rely on cloudy wine.
Number Twenty
Xī Nóng has left us for a long time,
and few in the world return to genuineness!
The busy old man of Lǔ,
patched things up to make them pure.
Although the phoenix did not arrive,
ritual and music were temporarily renewed.
The subtle sounds of the Zhū and Sì rivers ceased,
drifting until the tyrannical Qín.
What crime did the poems and books commit
that in one morning they became ashes and dust?
The petty old men,
were truly diligent in their work.
How is it that in later generations,
none are intimate with the Six Classics!
All day long, one drives the carriage,
but does not see where to inquire for the ford.
If one does not drink happily again,
one will vainly bear the kerchief on one's head.
I only regret that there are many errors,
but you should forgive a drunken man.
*Zhǐ Jiǔ* (Stopping Wine)
Living in towns and cities,
leisurely and free, stopping at will.
Sitting and stopping under a tall shade,
walking and stopping inside the wattle gate.
A good taste is stopping at garden mallows,
great joy is stopping at young children.
In my whole life, I have never stopped drinking wine,
stopping wine makes my emotions joyless.
Stopping in the evening, I cannot sleep peacefully,
stopping in the morning, I cannot rise.
Every day I want to stop it,
but stopping does not regulate my *yíng wèi*.
I only know that stopping is not joyful,
but I do not know that stopping benefits myself.
Only now do I feel that stopping is good,
and this morning I have truly stopped.
From now on, I will stop completely,
and will stop at the edge of Fúsāng.
A clear face will stop from holding a worried expression,
why only stop for ten thousand ages?

*Shù Jiǔ* (Narrating Wine)
Chóng Lí shines on the southern lands,
the sounds of singing birds are heard.
Although the autumn grass is not yet yellow,
the gentle breeze has long been divided.
White pebbles gleam on the long shore,
on the southern peak there are no remaining clouds;
Yùzhāng lifts its high gate,
and Chóng Huá's tomb is truly spiritual.
Shedding tears, I embrace my heart and sigh,
and prick up my ears to listen to the morning crow.
Divine lands offer fine grain,
and the western spirit tames it for me.
Zhū Liáng commanded the troops,
Qiān Shèng lost his life.
Shānyáng returned to the lower kingdom,
but still did not diligently establish his name.
Bǔ Shēng was good at herding this land,
and found happiness in not being a ruler.
Píng Wáng left the old capital,
and in the gorges received the remaining fragrance.
Shuāng Yáng was just said to nurture,
and the three-toed beast displayed its strange markings.
Wángzǐ loved the clear flute,
and at midday soared over the Hé and Fén rivers.
Zhū Gōng practiced with his nine teeth,
and lived in seclusion, far from worldly strife.
Within the towering western mountains,
repose is what I often cherish.
Heaven's countenance is eternally firm,
Pēng and Shāng are not in the same category.
*Zé Zǐ* (Admonishing Sons)
Shū Yǎn, Xuān Sì, Yōng Fèn, Duān Yì, Tōng Tóng,
in total five people;
Shū, Xuān, Yōng, Duān, Tōng,
are all nicknames.
*Zé Zǐ* (Admonishing Sons)
White hair covers both temples,
and my skin is no longer firm.
Although I have five sons,
none of them like paper and brush.
Ā Shū is already sixteen,
and is exceedingly lazy.
Ā Xuān is about to begin learning,
but does not love literary arts.
Yōng and Duān are thirteen years old,
and do not know six or seven.
Tōng, the youngest, is almost nine,
but only seeks pears and chestnuts.
If Heaven's decree is thus,
then let us advance the things in our cups.
*Yǒu Huì Ér Zuò Bìng Xù* (Written at a Gathering, with a Preface)
The old grain has already disappeared,
and the new grain has not yet risen.
I am quite like an old farmer,
and yet I encounter a year of disaster.
The days and months are still long,
and the suffering has not yet ended.
The work of a year
cannot be hoped for,
and the resources for morning and evening
barely suffice for smoke and fire.
It has only been ten days,
but I already think of hunger and want.
The year is drawing to a close,
and I sigh with lasting concern.
If I do not narrate this now,
how will later generations hear of it?
In my weak years, I encountered family poverty,
and now, in old age, I suffer even longer from hunger.
Beans and wheat are truly what I envy,
so who would dare to desire sweetness and fatness!
I am as hungry as one who has eaten only half a meal,
and in the heat of summer, I am tired of cold clothes.
The years are about to end,
how can I not be saddened by hardship?
I always admire the heart of those who give porridge,
and deeply hate the impropriety of covering one's face.
Can a mere "Alas, come!" be grudged?
To die in vain is but to abandon oneself.
Is this excess their desire?
Enduring poverty is what I have long resigned myself to.
To starve is enough!
In the past, I had many teachers.
*Là Rì* (The Day of the Year-End Sacrifice)
The wind and snow send off the remaining season,
but it does not matter, for the time is already harmonious.
Plum and willow trees are planted on either side of the gate,
and one branch has a beautiful flower.
I sing and you respond in agreement,
what is especially plentiful in the wine!
I cannot yet make clear how much,
but Zhāng Shān has a marvelous song.
